chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if the statues/images are on the garment, provided the image is removed from it."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in clothes with pictures or statues on them?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of praying in garments bearing images (tamasheel) provided the image is removed or altered, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the mere presence of an image does not invalidate prayer unless it is an idol or accompanied by specific prohibitions. It highlights the principle of ease in worship, distinguishing between the general prohibition of images in some contexts and their specific impact on the validity of salah. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-salah discussions regarding the purity and permissibility of clothing materials and decorations.
